title: Softmax and LayerNorm — November 25, 2026
body:
Softmax — resources, timing and accuracy

- For a 49-key row: 225 ALMs, 0 DSPs and 1 M10K (8192 bits). Measured HPS latency: INT8 5.51 µs; FP32 13.12 µs. Fabric RTL: 606 cycles, projected 8.08 µs at 75 MHz.
- On 10 local images, top-1 / top-5 predictions agreed 100% / 100% with FP32. INT8 relative RMSE: 6.56% on probabilities and 2.60% on attention context. Prediction agreement is not ground-truth accuracy.

LayerNorm — resources, timing and accuracy

- For a 192-channel token: 950 ALMs, 13 DSPs and 6 M10Ks (22016 bits). Measured HPS INT8 latency: 40.43 µs with exact correction or 158.13 µs with integer division; FP32: 7.76 µs. Fabric RTL: 3337 cycles, projected 44.49 µs at 75 MHz.
- On 10 local images, both FP32 and the INT8 replacement achieved 100% top-1 / top-5 accuracy against image labels. LayerNorm output relative RMSE was 3.49%. This is a small local test, not a full-dataset accuracy benchmark.

Per-image compute and transfer estimates

- Workload: 4704 Softmax rows × 49 scores and 784 LayerNorm tokens × 192 channels.
- HPS INT8: Softmax 25.93 + 2.51 = 28.44 ms; LayerNorm 31.70 + 1.25 = 32.95 ms (compute + estimated bulk transfer).
- Fabric: Softmax 38.01 + 2.01 = 40.02 ms; LayerNorm 34.88 + 0 = 34.88 ms, using the listed 0 ms LayerNorm transfer assumption.
- Combined HPS INT8 estimate: 61.39 ms; combined fabric estimate: 74.90 ms. Under these assumptions, fabric is 13.51 ms slower; offload has not demonstrated a speedup for this workload. These are operator-workload estimates, not measured full-model inference times.

Next steps

- Validate transfer assumptions and measure integrated board latency under matched conditions before choosing which operators to offload.
- Tables, downloadable CSVs and source screenshots are in ECE496 Files & Data: https://vit-fpga-wiki.pages.dev/#/files
